notes: The glass is thinner: the pane runs from about a third opaque to just over a half, where it used to run from a half to nearly nine tenths. The wallpaper is no longer a tint behind a sheet — it is what you look through.
And there is less milk in it. The panel is mixed toward white half as much, so what comes through is colour with a cool cast on top instead of a white haze. Thicker still reads colder, not chalkier.

The highlight moves now. The fixed corner sheen is a specular band that drifts across the pane on a slow loop, and it sits still for anyone who has Reduce motion on. That is the Settings preview, because the home-screen widget draws a colour and cannot carry a filter — the see-through part is what reaches your wallpaper.

The preview is a lens: a bright rim across the top, a soft one under the bottom, and a harder colour push behind it so the thinner glass has something to show. The type is a shade deeper to hold up at the new transparency.
The dial is untouched and still remembers where you leave it. Its caption is honest about the trade now: the thinner end is clearer, the thicker end is easier to read.
Nothing else moved — the eighteen other presets, fine-tune, follow-the-app-theme, the idle saver and the app's own Liquid glass mode are exactly as they were.
